sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert phonology and lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 485 pp. https://scholarspace.manoa.hawaii.edu/bitstream/10125/73354/1/
sources.note: Sec. 4.6 Yarawata (pp. 159-160): phoneme inventory /i u a/, /b t d k g m n l w y/, /b/ final devoicing, [s] allophone of /t/ next to /i/, epenthetic final vowel; nothing on stress. Sec. 1.5.1 'Stress' (pp. 31-32): stress described only for Mauwake, Pamosu, Usan; 'Unfortunately, the available data on stress in most languages are minimal or nonexistent'. Fn. 10 (p. 31): 'My analyses of Parawen, Ukuriguma, and Yarawata phonology are based solely on the phonetic transcriptions of Z'graggen's wordlists, so are extremely tentative.' Ch. 4 intro (p. 140): Yarawata data limited to Z'graggen (1980b) w…

sources.citation: Greenhill, S. J. (ed.). TransNewGuinea.org: Yarawata (362 entries, source Z'graggen 1980). https://transnewguinea.org/language/yarawata
sources.note: Nothing; retyped Z'graggen lexicon with length marks, no stress marks.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Northern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-31. Canberra: ANU. xvi+178 pp. (Yarawata = F17). http://sealang.net/archives/pl/pdf/
sources.note: Nothing. Intro sec. 7 (pp. viii-ix): 'The transcription is rendered semi-phonemic; i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted'; fluctuation table for Yarawata b~beta, d~r~y, s~ts; sec. 2 (p. vi): Yarawata-Parawen-Ukuriguma share >81% vocabulary. Wordlist forms carry vowel length but no stress marks (checked page image p. 20 = PDF p. 36: 'neck' kumʌːna, 'throat' marinʌma).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, Pacific Linguistics C-38, 569-612. http://sealang.net/archives/pl/pdf/
sources.note: Nothing; population F17 Yarawata 98, object-marker suffixing note for Numugenan languages (p. 589), comparative pronoun/lexical rows only.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. http://sealang.net/archives/pl/pdf/
sources.note: Sec. 1.3.3 (p. 6): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet' (all languages of the study). Yarawata appears only as a village of Ukuriguma UKU (sec. 2.22.24.14, p. 53: 'included into the figures of speakers, but disregarded in any other respect'). Wayapan Group typology (p. 54) segmental only; sec. 2.22.8 (p. 73) Adelbert Range Phylum: 'None of the languages appears to be tonal'. No stress placement statement.
Stub citing Pick 2020 only; no phonology.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2022. A reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert phonology and lexicon. In Epps, Law & Pat-El (eds), Historical Linguistics and Endangered Languages: Exploring Diversity in Language Change, 215-262. New York: Routledge.
